# `max-properties-increased`

maxProperties increased

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `max-properties-increased` (both directions), `max-properties-increased-in-request`, `max-properties-increased-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`maxProperties` increased.

## Why this default

In requests: more objects are valid. In responses: clients may receive larger objects than they expect.

## Example

From test case [`max-properties-increased`](../../test/cases/max-properties-increased/): maxProperties raised on a response object.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-       maxProperties: 5
+       maxProperties: 10
```

Findings:

- `max-properties-increased-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  max-properties-increased: warn
```

## How to fix

Check that clients handle the larger objects.
